name: Uniqueness of the Group Identity
description: A1 (∀y. e·y = y), A2 (∀x. x·f = x), A3 (single-valued) ⊢ e = f — the left identity equals the right identity, the classic e = e·f = f. A Beta, theory-relative theorem (Γ ⊢ φ from axioms) and the first fixture to exercise multi-line universal instantiation (A3's four lines to two constants at once) and equality-as-ligature. The derivation is original to Arisbe (the theorem is folklore); every step a real, attestable rule application.
